question: What is the primary goal of healthcare decontamination?

options.A: Enhancing the visual appearance of instruments
options.C: Lowering the financial cost of medical supplies

explanation: Decontamination targets harmful microbes to prevent them from spreading to patients and staff. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why is decontamination considered a bridge between clinical care and microbiology?

options.A: Patients perform microbiology tests before hospital admission.
options.B: Microscopes are mandatory in every patient ward.
options.C: Nurses must culture every instrument after cleaning it.
options.D: It requires applying microbiological principles to break infection chains.

explanation: Understanding how pathogens survive and spread helps nurses apply the correct decontamination methods. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which process removes organic soil and foreign material using water and detergents?
explanation: Cleaning is the vital first step that physically removes dirt and organic matter before disinfection or sterilization. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h2)

question: What distinguishes sterilization from disinfection?

options.A: Disinfection uses only high-temperature steam under pressure.
options.C: Sterilization is performed exclusively on human skin surfaces.
options.D: Sterilization destroys all microbial life including bacterial spores.

explanation: Only sterilization achieves the complete destruction of endospores, whereas standard disinfection leaves spores behind. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which Spaulding category requires complete sterilization before use?
explanation: Critical items enter sterile body cavities and tissues, demanding absolute freedom from all microbes through sterilization. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h3)

question: A blood pressure cuff touches only intact skin during patient assessment. How should it be classified?
explanation: Items contacting only intact skin present low infection risk and fall under the non-critical category requiring basic cleaning or low-level disinfection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is the most dependable physical method for sterilizing medical instruments?

options.D: Boiling water in an open pot

explanation: Moist heat under pressure penetrates materials effectively and destroys all microbial life, including spores. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why is ultraviolet radiation limited in its ability to disinfect complex rooms?

options.A: It can only function underwater in sealed containers.
options.B: It leaves a toxic chemical residue on all hard surfaces.
options.C: It automatically destroys all bacterial endospores instantly.
options.D: It requires a direct line of sight to be effective.

explanation: UV rays cannot bend around corners or penetrate shadowed areas, leaving untreated zones behind objects. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary difference between a disinfectant and an antiseptic?

options.A: Disinfectants contain alcohol, whereas antiseptics only contain water.
options.B: Antiseptics destroy bacterial spores while disinfectants cannot.
options.C: Antiseptics are strictly used for sterilizing surgical scalpel blades.
options.D: Disinfectants are for inanimate objects, while antiseptics are for living tissue.

explanation: Formulations differ because skin cannot tolerate the harsh chemical concentrations used on non-living surfaces. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h5)

question: What property of sodium hypochlorite requires nurses to use it carefully on metal instruments?

options.A: It neutralizes when exposed to room lighting.
options.B: It causes metal corrosion with prolonged contact.
options.C: It solidifies immediately upon touching stainless steel.
options.D: It evaporates too quickly to disinfect hard surfaces.

explanation: Chlorine solutions can pit and damage metal surgical tools if rinsing and drying are delayed. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h5)

question: What is the very first step to perform immediately after using surgical instruments?

options.A: Place them inside the high-pressure autoclave
options.B: Immerge them directly into concentrated bleach
options.C: Wipe off gross debris and keep items moist
options.D: Package them tightly in plastic nylon bags

explanation: Preventing blood and tissue from drying on instruments makes subsequent cleaning much easier and more effective. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h6)

question: Why is drying instruments thoroughly before sterilization or high-level disinfection essential?

options.A: It makes the metal tools change color for easy sorting.
options.B: It ensures that bacterial endospores multiply rapidly.
options.C: It prevents water from diluting chemicals or causing rust.
options.D: It helps the instruments cool down before packaging.

explanation: Excess moisture interferes with chemical potency and promotes oxidation and rust on metal tools. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which PPE item is specifically required during manual instrument cleaning to prevent chemical splashes and injury?

options.A: Lead-lined apron and radiation dosimetry badge
options.B: Disposable paper cap and soft canvas shoes
options.C: Sterile surgical gown and latex examination gloves
options.D: Heavy-duty utility gloves and eye protection

explanation: Utility gloves protect hands from sharp edges and harsh detergents, while eye protection prevents chemical splashes. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of having an operational eye-wash station in a decontamination room?

options.A: To clean surgical instruments before manual scrubbing
options.B: To provide drinking water for exhausted staff members
options.C: To test the water pressure of the hospital plumbing
options.D: To flush out chemical splashes from eyes immediately

explanation: Immediate irrigation is critical to minimize ocular damage when caustic disinfectants splash into the eyes. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h7)

question: Which monitoring indicator uses resistant bacterial spores to confirm actual sterilization?
explanation: Biological indicators contain actual heat-resistant spores to prove the sterilizer successfully destroyed living microorganisms. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h8)

question: What do chemical indicator strips demonstrate when they change color?

options.A: The package was exposed to specific sterilizing conditions.
options.B: The staff members followed proper hand hygiene steps.
options.C: The instruments inside are completely sterile and safe.
options.D: The autoclave machine has no mechanical faults at all.

explanation: Chemical indicators show exposure to parameters like heat or steam, but they do not guarantee absolute sterility like biological tests. [learn more](GST114_U2_T9#GST114_U2_T9_h8)
